# Large source maps need bounded section metadata as well as bounded text

The architecture study exposed a local index integration problem: splitting a large record into small text sections still repeated the complete record path list in each section's metadata and search input. This increased cache size and could make a returned section exceed the console response budget.

The local `sectionMetadata()` helper keeps at most eight relevant paths for a section. It keeps the complete paths on the immutable parent record and records their total count when the section omits paths. `indexSections()` indexes the section paths instead of every parent path. `searchKnowledge()` also bounds metadata when returning a legacy cached section.

The text offsets, section IDs, embedding inputs, record IDs, copy grouping, and full source paths are retained. `SECTION_VERSION` remains 1 because this fix does not change the text boundaries or embedding input. Existing cached rows are not automatically compacted on disk. A rebuilt disposable index uses the smaller representation for new sections.

Validation: nine focused Node tests passed on Node.js 26.3.1. The new large-map test checks 500 source paths, retrieval through a correction copy, legacy section metadata, and unchanged parent paths. Existing section, index-lookup, and retrieval-trace tests also passed. Product tests and embeddings were not run.

## Publication and limits

This is an uncommitted local fix applied on top of other ongoing console changes. The source hashes below identify the tested working files; the base Git revision alone does not contain this implementation. Do not assume a fresh upstream clone already has it. The shared knowledge repository contains this evidence, not retrieval code or generated indexes. The implementation belongs in tb-tools.

A plain symbol lookup can still rank a structural map ahead of a behavior note. Richer queries about the state, transaction, error, or test contract help find the checked chain. The patch does not claim to solve semantic caller resolution or all ranking problems.
